ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 driver-cancelled no-show fee; no refund and no account action on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip alleging a rider no-show, so NS-0 routes the case into NS-1, and the trace settles all three limbs: arrival confirmation by driver tap at 17:19:15 [F6], that tap 41 m from the pickup — inside the 200 m data-layer radius [F6, F1], and 220 s (3 min 40 s) continuously inside the radius after the tap until the 17:22:55 cancellation, above the >180 s requirement [F6, F4]. The rider's central argument — that NS-1(iii) counts only post-tap time and that F6 shows only 3 min 40 s — actually satisfies the clause: NS-1(iii) requires more than 3 minutes (≥3:01) of continuous presence at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, and 3 min 40 s is more than that, so the argument is self-defeating [F6][NS-1]. The rider's alternative reading, anchoring the wait at the driver's 17:19 chat message [F9] rather than the tap, has no basis: NS-1(iii) anchors on the "I'm Here" tap, not on a chat message [F9, F10][NS-1].

Because (i)(ii)(iii) all hold, NS-2 is not triggered and the $6.61 cancellation fee on the fare record stands [F7, F4][NS-1, NS-2]. The rider's complaint that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is a statement unsupported by any GPS or timeline fact; no record shows the rider at the pickup point at any time, and the system records override the uncorroborated narrative here [F2, F3, F5][NS-1]. The driver's post-trip statement [F12] is a claim needing no weight, since the GPS and timeline independently establish the limbs [F2, F6][NS-1].

No safety element arises: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint — F9 is an ordinary arrival notice, F10 an ordinary cancellation notice, F12 a factual account, and the complaint alleges only an unfair fee — none contains any threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9, F10, F11, F12][SAFE-1, SAFE-2]. No account flag is warranted: RD-6 requires a route-deviation case with an established RD-1 violation, which this is not, and the driver's 2 upheld no-show outcomes against 1124 trips in 90 days [F17] is not "repeated" conduct of the kind RD-6/NS-2 address; profile facts cannot decide or add an action here [F17][NS-1, RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: NS-1(iii) requires more than 3 minutes (≥3:01) of continuous presence within 200 m after the arrival confirmation; F6 records 3 min 40 s (220 s) of exactly that, so the wait is satisfied, not failed [F6][NS-1].

The rider reads the 17:22 chat message [F10] as the clock anchor, but NS-1(iii) anchors on the 'I'm Here' tap [F6], not on a chat message, and the pre-tap stationary period [F3] is irrelevant because the post-tap period alone exceeds the threshold [F6][NS-1].
NS-2 applies only when one of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails; the trace settles all three as passing — tap at 17:19:15 within 200 m at 41 m, and 220 s inside the radius after the tap [F6][F1][NS-1, NS-2].
The $6.61 fee is correctly recorded [F7] but the refund condition of NS-2 is not met, and NS-7's voucher form only governs refunds that are otherwise payable [F7][NS-1, NS-2, NS-7].

The driver's 2 upheld no-show outcomes against 1124 trips in 90 days [F17] does not establish a violation in this case, and RD-6 requires an established RD-1/NS violation before any account flag [F17][RD-6, NS-2].

Accepted in outcome but note the rider's uncorroborated statement that she came out a minute after cancellation is not disproved by any GPS fact; it simply carries no record support, so the driver's no-show case rests on the settled NS-1 limbs [F4, F7, F6][NS-0, NS-1, NS-2].
